reasoning_traces.think:
The core distinction lies in how expectations are formed: mnemonization encodes past experiences into abstract representations, while perception reflects real-time sensory engagement. These two forms of expectation operate under different conditional dependencies—M depends on S_past, whereas P depends on S_present. The duality implies that both must coexist for optimal inference. In failure modes, either operator may dominate or fail due to lack of conditioning data. This leads to a structured kernel where M and P interact through shared object representations, enabling dynamic adjustment of belief states based on new evidence or recall. The formalism supports recursive updating and probabilistic reasoning across time scales.
